# intutic_guardrail <Badge type="tip" text="Cloud" />

A policy guardrail written as code, managed through `/api/v1/policy-guardrails/guardrails`. It is held to the Guardrail IR and the validator a guardrail extracted from a policy document passes, without the checks that compare a model's output with the passage it cites. A new guardrail starts `PROPOSED`, like an extracted one: it enforces and measures nothing until a member approves it for shadow, and promotion to `ENFORCING` waits on shadow evidence through the same review actions (the dashboard, `intutic guardrails approve-shadow` and `promote`). Terraform manages the rule, not its lifecycle. Changing `name` or `description` edits the guardrail in place and keeps its evidence. Changing any IR attribute creates the next version under a new id, `PROPOSED` with no evidence, and retires this one (undoing what it wrote, if it was an enforcing allowed-models or egress guardrail); the plan shows the new `version` and `status` before you apply. Destroying it retires it; its history is kept. The plan also asks the API to run the full validator, so a rule the API would refuse fails at plan time. Needs an OWNER or ADMIN key.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A hook rule: the harness gates block `terraform apply` once the guardrail
# is enforcing. It starts PROPOSED; approve it for shadow and promote it on
# evidence in the guardrail review (or with `intutic guardrails`).
resource "intutic_guardrail" "reviewed_apply" {
  name         = "Reviewed terraform apply"
  description  = "Production applies need a reviewed plan."
  kind         = "hook_rule"
  title        = "Reviewed plan before terraform apply"
  tools        = ["Bash"]
  arg_contains = ["terraform apply"]
}

# A front-matter rule the proxy enforces, for contractors only.
resource "intutic_guardrail" "no_web_fetch" {
  name  = "No web fetch for contractors"
  kind  = "deny_tools"
  tools = ["WebFetch"]
  roles = ["contractor"]
}

# A workspace setting: on promotion it narrows the workspace's allowed models.
resource "intutic_guardrail" "approved_models" {
  name   = "Approved models"
  kind   = "allowed_models"
  models = ["claude-sonnet-4-5", "gpt-4o"]
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `kind` (String) The IR kind: `allowed_models`, `deny_tools`, `egress_allow`, `forbid_after`, `forbid_with`, `hook_rule`, `max_calls`, `requires_before`, `review_before`, `wasm_predicate`. The attributes below say which kinds take them.
- `name` (String) One-line label, at most 80 characters, without surrounding whitespace.

### Optional

- `arg_contains` (List of String) `hook_rule`: fire only when the serialised tool input contains every one of these literals (at most 4, each 1 to 64 characters, no tab, newline, double quote or backslash).
- `arg_not_contains` (List of String) `hook_rule`: fire only when the tool input contains none of these literals (same limits as `arg_contains`).
- `description` (String) What the rule is for, at most 480 characters. A hook rule's block message carries it where an extracted rule carries its quote (the `name` stands there when this is unset).
- `first` (String) `requires_before`, `forbid_after` (required): the first token; differs from `then`.
- `hosts` (List of String) `egress_allow` (required, 1 to 32): hosts (`api.example.com`), suffixes (`.example.com`) or IPv4 addresses and CIDRs no wider than /8.
- `limit` (Number) `max_calls` (required): the most calls allowed, 1 to 1000.
- `models` (List of String) `allowed_models` (required, 1 to 32): model ids, compared exactly as the proxy compares them.
- `predicate` (String) `wasm_predicate` (required): the predicate in the closed rule DSL, as JSON (`jsonencode({ all = [...] })`). Its verdict is always re-ask.
- `rationale` (String) `wasm_predicate` (required): why the rule re-asks, at most 480 characters.
- `roles` (List of String) Every kind but `allowed_models` and `egress_allow`: the lower-case roles the rule applies to (at most 8). Unset, it applies to everyone.
- `taint` (String) `forbid_with` (required): `secrets()` or `pii()`.
- `then` (String) `requires_before`, `forbid_after` (required): the second token.
- `title` (String) `hook_rule`, `wasm_predicate` (required): the title, 1 to 80 characters, that starts the block message.
- `token` (String) `max_calls`, `forbid_with` (required): the tool name or action token.
- `tokens` (List of String) `review_before` (required, 1 to 16): tool names or action tokens.
- `tools` (List of String) `hook_rule` (required, 1 to 8), `deny_tools` (required, 1 to 16): tool names (`Bash`, `mcp__github__create_issue`) or action tokens. A known harness tool is written in its canonical case (`WebFetch`, not `webfetch`).

### Read-Only

- `enforcing_fires` (Number) Times this version acted while enforcing.
- `id` (String) The guardrail id (`pgr_…`). Changes when an IR change creates the next version.
- `provenance` (String) Always `authored`. An extracted guardrail cannot be managed or imported by this resource.
- `shadow_evaluations` (Number) Shadow evaluations this version has accumulated; promotion needs the threshold the API reports.
- `shadow_would_act` (Number) Shadow evaluations on which this version would have acted.
- `status` (String) `PROPOSED`, `SHADOW`, `ENFORCING` or `REJECTED`. Moved by the review actions, never by Terraform.
- `supersedes` (String) The id of the version this one replaced, or null.
- `target` (String) The enforcer the rule is projected into: `hook_rule`, `sop_front_matter`, `wasm_rule` or `workspace_setting`.
- `version` (Number) 1 for a new guardrail; each IR change creates the next.

## Import

```shell
# Import an authored guardrail by id. An extracted guardrail cannot be imported.
terraform import intutic_guardrail.reviewed_apply pgr_0123456789abcdef
```
